function.name: reply
function.description: Final answer with requestCoverage, language override or raw/debug metadata. Stream ordinary prose as assistant text. Call alone, no preamble; ends the turn. brief is concise; detailed/debug preserve explicitly requested content and require an exact user scopeQuote. Brief rejects boilerplate, internal fields and Chinese for an English request; correct rejected answers. Use task_reply only for explicit progress questions and ask_user for missing decisions.

requestCoverage.description: Independent outcomes; keep constraints together. current=handoff; delegated needs taskId.

function.name: conversation_history
function.description: Restore this conversation's earlier assistant and tool records for this turn when a reference, decision, exact quote or result is missing. No extra model rewrite or mutation. Forgotten content stays excluded. Do not read history for a self-contained question.

function.name: ask_user
function.description: Ask only when a real decision is missing. Supply 2-4 concrete options, recommended first. Never ask permission again for an already authorized session message or task. This ends the turn and waits for the user's selection; call this tool alone, then stop.

function.name: task_reply
function.description: Answer a question asking ONLY whether ONE referenced task is finished/running. Use this instead of composing a status answer from history. Reads actual task state and delivers one short answer in the user's language, ending this turn without another model call. Call alone without a text preamble. taskId is required: resolve the referenced task from context. Never substitute a queue overview. Completion callbacks must report actual findings, file links and pending acceptance or blockers with assistant text or reply; downloadable files do not replace an outcome summary. For detailed results, explanations, raw/debug fields, mixed requests or other languages use task_status instead.

languageQuote.description: Only for an explicit request to reply in a different language, copy the user's exact language instruction.

function.name: task_queue_reply
function.description: Answer ONLY a whole-queue question such as whether any tasks are running. Never use for one referenced task. Read current queue state and deliver a short answer, ending this turn. Call alone without a preamble. Use task_reply with taskId for a particular task; task_status for details or mixed requests.

function.name: delegate
function.description: Delegate with routing assessment and explicitExecutor (user choice or null). Host routes bounded work to native, complex work to an available professional. Source-backed user choices win; omit legacy executor. Main session targets send directly, including legacy sessions without callbacks: delivery only. Other targets return queued background_task/taskId, not completion. Task/native-branch IDs are not session IDs. Edits, additions and missing deliverables of tracked work use task_steer, even after completion; do not delegate a new task into its workspace. The original executor choice remains bound without a fresh quote. New coding tasks resolve real Roami projects; Git projects use worktrees. Recall scoped work habits; workspacePreference references active memoryId/revision/quote with optional quoted base/remote. fromMessageId forks completed checkpoints only.

goal.description: For a self-contained public lookup, use the user's question verbatim. Do not add provider checklists, result counts or source examples. Resolve missing references only when needed.

title.description: Short topic; keep full requirements, paths and steps in goal.

requestComplete.description: Required for the whole user message: false while any independent part remains (including target discovery); true only on the last handoff. Never wait or poll after acceptance.

requestCoverage.description: Independent outcomes; keep constraints together. current=handoff; delegated needs taskId.

explicitExecutor.description: Required: the user's requested executor; null only with no user choice. Never hide a requested CLI in goal or relabel it as native.

quote.description: Exact user quote requesting this native CLI model. Omit model to use the CLI default.

complexity.description: Execution burden: complex requires autonomous planning, exploring unknowns, coordinating dependencies or feedback-driven revision. bounded requires a procedure known BEFORE work, not just a known symptom or narrow goal. Must agree with complexityBasis/routingExplanation. Finite deliverables can be complex.

userQuote.description: Exact source quote for a non-null explicitExecutor only. Omit when explicitExecutor is null; this is not a general task quote.

requiredCapabilities.description: Declare required cli:COMMAND availability and, for native tasks, model:CAPABILITY input support (for example model:images). Native model requirements use the saved Worker route; Main support does not transfer. Resolve needed evidence in Main before handing off execution when only Main supports it.

resourceOnly.description: External lookup without preparing a coding workspace. Enabled Skills, MCP and CLI remain available. User-authorized local host operations use bash scope=host in Main.

target.description: Session: kind=session, exact sessionId (+nodeId/label), no directory/workspaceId/base/remote overrides. Project: kind=project, discovered projectId; workspaceId reuses work without path/base/remote overrides. New native work: kind=new_session omits directory for a private writable task directory; preserve a user-selected existing directory. Never use baseDir for new_session. Only a user-requested new project uses new_project, name (+existing absolute baseDir). Never invent IDs or paths.

function.name: tool_list
function.description: Discover extra Skills, MCP and CLI capabilities; built-in tools are already supplied. Filter by name/intent/category and paginate. Returns skill:// paths or exact bash argv and schemas. Known operations can run directly. This is a local capability directory, not web results or service pricing.

function.name: read
function.description: Read files within bound/configured roots, skill://NAME[/references/FILE.md] or artifact://ID. Load relevant references only. First-page local images reach Main or Worker when that role is configured for image input; other roles receive metadata.

function.name: edit
function.description: Apply one exact file replacement after checking expectedSha256. Use read first; ambiguous or changed files are rejected.

function.name: write
function.description: Atomically write a workspace file. New file: prefer expectedSha256 as JSON null (unquoted). Existing file: use the exact sha256 returned by read. Never overwrite unrelated changes.

expectedSha256.description: New file: JSON null, without quotes. The literal string "null" also means exclusive creation only. Existing file: exact sha256 from read. Example: {"path":"answer.txt","expectedSha256":null,"content":"Answer"}. Never guess a hash.

function.name: bash
function.description: Execute discovered Roami CLI operations. Main has no implicit shell workspace. For user-authorized local machine operations, set scope=host and omit cwd; host scope is general execution in a temporary working directory, not a read-only sandbox. For project code or file deliverables, keep workspace scope and delegate to a worker with the user-selected directory, or an automatic private directory for new native work. Registered permissions and execution receipts remain enforced.

scope.description: Host scope is for user-authorized local machine operations in Main, without cwd or a task workspace. It is general execution, not a read-only sandbox. Workspace scope preserves configured roots and bound task directories.

builtins.description: Append the user's message or work instructions to one exact existing live session. Works with legacy Codex/Claude sessions without lifecycle callbacks. Returns delivery only, NOT task completion. replyExpected=true includes a durable dispatchId and a local CLI return channel for executor reports; executionTracked=false means no provider lifecycle proof. Wait for the report in Main, never claim completion from delivery. Use immediately when the user asks to message, hand work to, or continue an existing session; the request authorizes sending, so do not ask again. Resolve the destination using available context or discovery, never guess among ambiguous matches. For a new session/project or tracked task use delegate instead. Do not retry unknown outcomes.

builtins.name: target_search

Use one exact unique match directly; never guess among duplicate names. session_send appends to legacy sessions; tracked task continuation requires lifecycle callbacks.

builtins.name: target_resolve
builtins.description: Resolve an exact project ID or live session ID/name/label; duplicate labels fail. Liveness does not prove a task finished or stopped.

builtins.description: Continue a known tracked task with additional user requirements at its actual revision. Preserves its executor and source; waits for stop proof. This cannot switch executors or use a tmux sessionId. Queue acceptance is not completion.

builtins.description: Read delegated progress in this conversation. A progress question needs only state and essential blockers, not a repeated report. Use includeResult=true only when the user asks for prior detailed/full results; the stored executor report is not fresh retrieval. Optionally filter by exact taskId.

builtins.name: reminder_create
builtins.description: Create only an explicitly requested reminder. kind=daily_brief schedules a short model-generated brief of yesterday's recorded conversation activity; it requires dailyAt and has a separate background budget. Otherwise choose exactly one: afterSeconds, whenMs (UTC epoch milliseconds), dailyAt (HH:MM in timezone). Return persisted nextDueMs, never claim device delivery. Ask if time is ambiguous.

builtins.name: reminder_list
builtins.description: List current conversation reminders and the runtime clock; bounded to 20, active first.

builtins.name: reminder_cancel

builtins.name: host_processes
builtins.description: Read current local machine process CPU/memory usage, load average, memory and swap. Returns top CPU and RSS processes with PID and elapsed time; ps CPU is a lifetime average per core, not an instantaneous sample. Runs on the Agent runtime host/namespace, not the user's phone or remote nodes. No workspace, project, shell argv or browser task required. Command names only; no arguments or environment. Unavailable metrics stay null. Read-only; cannot kill processes or modify the host.

Reuse the same previewId/option/name to recover the same successful installation; expired receipts require preview again.
